parsed.explanation: Parent regime creates tier-1 traveler exposures: binary passport policy, entry scrutiny for document/presentation discrepancies, ban on gender-identity use of government-funded facilities, and documented severe custody harm including hormone removal and abuse in immigration detention. Courts and litigation provide partial recourse and several orders are enjoined, but do not reliably prevent these practices. The state adds a schools/colleges birth-certificate facility law, yet it has no enforcement mechanism or criminal penalty and general public facilities are not banned locally; no state anti-discrimination statute, though 33 municipalities provide some protection. Hostile official framing and public support for birth-sex documents increase risk if outed, while functioning rule of law and absence of a general presentation offence keep it above severe/high-risk anchors. Net: elevated-to-high risk, approximately 0.39.
